metadata.title: Artificial Neural Network and Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System Hybridized Models in the Sustainable Integration of Language and Mathematics Skills: The Case of Singaporeand Hong Kong

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study does not analyze individual-level PISA microdata with sampling weights; instead, it performs content analysis of national curricula and then uses ANN/ANFIS to relate curriculum-derived language themes to PISA 2018 mathematics/reading outcomes for Singapore and Hong Kong. Because the dependent variable is based on PISA scores reported at the country level (not student-level PVs), complex survey weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) are not applicable in the usual ILSA sense. The manuscript also does not report any use of replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) or any explicit complex-survey adjustment. Therefore, readers should interpret model fit (RMSE/R²) as descriptive associations between curriculum content frequencies and published PISA outcomes rather than as population-representative estimates from a weighted student sample.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not report a missing-data strategy because it does not perform an ILSA-style student-level analysis with item nonresponse or PV-based achievement scores. Instead, it uses document/content analysis to derive counts of language-skill themes from curricula and then models relationships to published PISA 2018 scores for two countries. As a result, the typical PV generation/combining and missingness mechanisms for student responses are not part of the analysis pipeline described in the manuscript.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level PISA sample is constructed. The study uses document analysis of Singapore and Hong Kong native-language and mathematics curricula to extract language-skill themes and their frequencies, then compares/inputs these curriculum-derived theme counts to published PISA 2018 mathematics/reading scores for Singapore and Hong Kong. The ANN/ANFIS modeling uses a data split of 70% training, 15% testing, and 15% validation, but the manuscript does not specify any additional inclusion/exclusion criteria at the student level because no student microdata are analyzed.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (country-level outcomes) + Singapore/Hong Kong curricula (content-derived language themes); ANN Model 1
main_findings.target_variable: Language skills (native-language curriculum) predicted from verbal skills themes
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (country-level outcomes) together with Singapore/Hong Kong curriculum content-derived language themes, the study leveraged verbal skills theme frequency and PISA 2018 scores to predict language skills (native-language curriculum outcomes), finding that the relationship was insufficient with R² ≈ 0.35 and RMSE ≈ 17.64. This indicates that curriculum language-theme coverage alone may not strongly explain cross-country differences in language-related achievement outcomes, so policy efforts should also consider broader instructional, classroom, and student factors beyond curriculum content.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (country-level outcomes) + Singapore/Hong Kong curricula (content-derived language themes); ANFIS Model 2
main_findings.target_variable: Language skills (native-language curriculum) predicted from verbal skills themes
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (country-level outcomes) together with Singapore/Hong Kong curriculum content-derived language themes, the study leveraged verbal skills theme frequency and PISA 2018 scores to predict language skills (native-language curriculum outcomes), finding that the relationship remained insufficient but improved slightly with R² ≈ 0.40 and RMSE ≈ 12.43. This indicates that hybrid ANN–fuzzy modeling captures some nonlinearity in the curriculum-to-outcome association, but the low fit suggests that additional determinants (e.g., teaching practices, resources, and student background) are likely needed for stronger explanatory/predictive models.

data.outcome_summary: The study investigates how language skills relate to mathematics success by combining (i) content analysis of Singapore and Hong Kong native-language and mathematics curricula and (ii) AI modeling that links curriculum-derived language-theme frequencies to published PISA 2018 outcomes for the two countries. It builds two predictive models: an ANN (Model 1) and an ANFIS hybrid model (Model 2), both implemented in MATLAB 2019a, with a 70%/15%/15% train–test–validation split. Model fit is modest: ANN yields RMSE = 17.6385 and R² = 0.353954, while ANFIS yields RMSE = 12.42771 and R² = 0.397867, and both are interpreted as insufficient relationships. The analysis is limited because it does not use student-level PISA microdata (no PVs or survey weights) and relies on a very small effective dataset (two countries), which the authors also cite as a likely reason for poor performance. Consequently, the results should be read as descriptive associations between curriculum content and country-level PISA outcomes rather than causal effects.
